programmes.d: Maya's article about Woody Allen catches the eye of an impostor.
Jack must prove himself worthy in order to get his young daughter admitted to a prestigious private school.
Maya's efforts to do something nice for a janitor backfires.
Elliott vows to use a high school teacher's funeral to prove something to his old classmates.
When Al and Peg decide to go on vacation, Steve and Marcy volunteer to take care of their kids, Bud and Kelly. But, their enthusiasm changes when the kids throw a huge party at the Rhoades' house.

Al invites Steve to play poker with his friends but ends up losing his paycheck to Al. Avoiding telling the truth to Marcy fails as Al plans to use his winnings to buy a fishing rod. Ultimately, Marcy enlists the help of Peggy to stop him.

When the owner of the shoe store is in a near-fatal plane crash, Al decides that it is time to get some recognition from his boss or quit his job. After quitting, Al returns to the shoe store, but not without a surprise.

Marcy freaks out when she begins having erotic dreams about Al after a heated argument about men vs women, and wonders whether she is actually sexually attracted to Al. Haunted by her dreams, Marcy ultimately comes to a conclusion and confronts Al.
When Doug has a bad toothache and winds up needing root canal, he finds out that Carrie used to have a crush on his dentist, Dr. Farber (Tim Matheson).
After their neighbors hear Doug & Carrie in a big fight, Carrie tries to convince the neighbors, Mike and Debi that they are better than that; Arthur gets Spence to let him ride the subway for free.
Doug gets Arthur to accompany him in his bed because he cannot sleep without Carrie.
Deacon complains to Doug about how much Kirby hates football, so he gets Doug to play football again to encourage him.
After Evelyn and Teddy become engaged, Charlie struggles to fight his attraction to Teddy's daughter, Courtney, Charlie's soon-to-be stepsister.
While trying to help Jake get over a breakup, Alan discovers that it was Charlie who stole his high school girlfriend. Alan seeks revenge on Charlie.
Seeing Alan not fully passionate about his relationship, Charlie coaches Alan in the fine art of breaking up with a woman.
Rose (recurring guest star MELANIE LYNSKEY), Charlie's lovable stalker, is back from England and takes strange care of a very sick Charlie.
Alan dates one of his ex-wife's friends, who reveals a secret about Judith's sex life. Recurring guest star RYAN STILES appears as Judith's second husband.
Charlie goes with Jake on a double date and sets Alan up with a prostitute. Recurring guest star MELANIE LYNSKEY appears as Rose.
While railing on the evils of Beanie Babies, Becker gets annoyed when an overly friendly delivery guy named Todd stops by the diner.
Becker throws his back out at home while trying to close a stuck window.
Becker has a fear that midgets bring him bad luck and is spooked by the new water guy, who happens to be vertically challenged.
Becker promises a friend that he will write a medical article for him, but gets frustrated with numerous distractions.
Becker learns that an elderly patient, Mr. Fowler, has suffered from a heart attack and calls his daughter to tell her the bad news.
Becker yells at a woman for letting her child cry uncontrollably, then rants about her bad parenting skills.
Becker is outraged as he tells the gang at the diner that someone broke into his apartment and stole his computer.
Becker starts off the day in a cranky mood when he finds a stray cat in his office, which apparently crawled through a broken window.

Helen throws her first Christmas party and all of her guests have their wallets stolen.
Helen and Joe baby-sit their friend's little girl and dump their childhood neuroses on her.
Joe and Brian are reunited with their grandfather, Jack Hackett, who Helen and Casey discover is an imposter.
R.J., Roy Biggins' estranged gay son, returns to Nantucket to celebrate his father's birthday and confronts him about his lifestyle.
Carrie is invited to her company's retreat for the first time and is overcome with excitement.
As Doug and Carrie's plane makes an unexpectedly rough landing, Doug takes the only available oxygen mask for himself and doesn't think twice about Carrie.
Doug decides to buy a pumpkin to get into the Halloween spirit, but as soon as Arthur sees it, he smashes it and banishes the celebration of Halloween.
As Arthur prepares to undergo heart surgery, Carrie discovers something that he did years ago that drastically affected her life.
When Andi and Marcy realize they were rivals in high school, Adam and Don are dragged into the feud and forced to take sides.
When Adam and Andi have the dreaded "talk" with Teddy and Kate, their awkward approach makes the kids horribly uncomfortable.
When Andi forces Adam to hang out with Lowell, Don feels left out and Andi has to make peace between them.
When Adam and Andi's babysitter cancels on Valentine's Day, they try to survive leaving Kate in charge at home for the first time.
After Alan and Charlie tell Evelyn that none of her acquaintances will mourn her when she dies, she bitterly ignores them for a few weeks.
When Jake starts covering his walls with posters of sexy women, Alan realizes that his son is almost grown up. He makes a last-minute attempt at father-son bonding.
As Judith and Herb's wedding nears, Charlie gets close to Herb's witty sister, Myra. Judith orders Alan to make Charlie stop pursuing Myra.
While Alan prepares Jake for Judith's wedding, Charlie continues his fling with Herb's sister, Myra. Charlie gets a surprise from Myra after admitting that he truly likes her.
Bill thinks he's been cheated by his new health club; the staff discovers a secret about Dave's past.
Lisa balks at being the Cutest Reporter in New York; Bill starts his own anti-rap music crusade.
Bill's relentless sarcasm leads to Matthew experimenting with his own dark side; Jimmy looks to Catherine for help beating a crooked card dealer.
Jimmy's new employee policy covering harassment backfires and brings work at the station to a standstill.
Maya tries proving herself to a successful college roommate; Jack's birthday sets Finch and Nina to fighting over who can find the best present.
